correctness.rationale: The proof-consequence closure is a permitted arbitrary set operator in Nishimura semantics. Finite-support derivability gives an exact bridge between closure membership and boxed membership in the canonical maximal consistent set. M, C, N, K and 4 are preserved by composing finite supports with their axioms. D is preserved because two opposite closure members would combine to make a finite subset of the consistent canonical set derive the conjunction forbidden by D. Restricting the canonical set to the finite augmented subformula set of one non-theorem leaves a finite generator and preserves every frame-condition argument.

evidence: Nishimura explicitly imposes no extensivity, monotonicity, or idempotence on the closure map, proves singleton completeness for M/C/N/K, and names D and 4 among the first prospective extensions.

Kogure--Kurahashi require an ordinary closure operator; their N is necessitation, while D and 4 have the same membership forms used here. Their finite completeness theorem excludes simultaneous necessitation and D, and the simultaneous case is handled by a different canonical construction.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The older D/4 theorems live in a materially different semantic and proof-theoretic regime. The present theorem neither follows from their stronger closure-operator axioms nor from their necessitation-based logic family, and Nishimura explicitly separates his broad closure notion from theirs.

originality.rationale: The primary source proves one-world completeness only for M/C/N/K and explicitly lists D and 4 as prospective extensions. The closest older paper treats D and 4 under conventional closure operators and with N denoting necessitation, not Nishimura's axiom Box-top. It does not cover the arbitrary-operator no-rule M/K hierarchy or imply the all-selection singleton theorem.

The theorem resolves both simultaneously for every no-inference-rule selection and preserves the strongest finite feature of the source, a one-world finite-generator countermodel.
